system_overview: Northwind Health is replacing its in-house payroll module with PayStream, a SaaS payroll product run by PayStream Pty Ltd. Northwind's HRIS stays the system of record and sends PayStream a nightly extract of employee, salary, bank account and tax file number data. Staff sign in through Entra ID, PayStream posts payroll journals to the finance general ledger, and a payroll administrator carries the payment file to the bank portal by hand.

This review supports the decision to go live for the first pay run. It found six open threats, all at the points where Northwind's systems and processes meet the vendor's product. The most significant are two shared local administrator accounts that bypass single sign-on, and the nightly extract, which sits on an integration host for thirty days alongside an SFTP key that has never been rotated.

key_components.name: PayStream administration console
key_components.why: Controls bank details and pay runs. Two shared local accounts reach it with a password alone.

key_components.name: Integration host
key_components.why: Holds the full employee extract for thirty days and the key that can upload data to PayStream.

key_components.name: PayStream platform
key_components.why: Holds all payroll data. Northwind depends on the vendor's controls and cannot currently see vendor support access.

key_components.name: Bank portal
key_components.why: The last check before money moves. The payment file reaches it by hand through a laptop.

next_steps.step: Remove the shared local administrator accounts or lock one down as a break-glass account, before go-live.
Move the SFTP key into a vault and stop keeping the extract on the integration host.
Confirm with PayStream whether webhook signing is on, then enable and verify it.
Obtain the vendor's SOC 2 Type II report and its support access log.
Add PayStream to the leaver process and reconcile accounts against HR records.

approach: We reviewed Northwind's solution architecture and context diagram and PayStream's security overview, then held an architecture walkthrough with Northwind's payroll and integration leads to fill the gaps the documents left.

From that we built a draft threat model, classified the threats with STRIDE, and walked it through with Northwind in a validation call. That call confirmed the architecture, corrected one control, added one threat and agreed the risk ratings using Northwind's risk matrix.

activities.description: Design documentation, context diagram and vendor security overview.
Workshop with Northwind's payroll systems lead and integration engineer.
System model, trust boundaries, threats, reported controls and open questions.
Draft model reviewed, corrected and rated with Northwind.
Recommendations, verification plan and this report.

review_coverage: All supplied design, vendor and workshop material was reviewed in full. PayStream's SOC 2 Type II report and the bank portal's approval configuration were requested but not available.
limitations: This assessment is based on documentation and workshops. No source code, configuration or running system was examined.
PayStream's internal controls are as the vendor describes them; its SOC 2 Type II report was not available.
The bank portal's approval configuration was not seen.

assumptions.statement: PayStream's description of its own controls is accurate.
assumptions.if_wrong: Threats involving the vendor's platform would be more likely; obtain the SOC 2 report to test this.

assumptions.statement: The corporate network is the only route to the administration console.
assumptions.if_wrong: Local accounts would be reachable from the internet, raising the likelihood of T-001 and T-006.

assumptions.statement: The bank approver checks more than the payment total.
assumptions.if_wrong: Nothing would detect an altered payment file before release.

T-001.title: Shared local administrator accounts bypass single sign-on
T-001.impact: Whoever holds one of these passwords controls payroll: they could change bank details and redirect salaries, and the shared account would not show who did it.
T-001.response_note: Agreed by Northwind in the validation call on 13 November 2026.
T-001.coverage_note: Single sign-on with multi-factor authentication covers normal access, but the local accounts sign in with a password and sit outside it.

T-002.title: Nightly extract and SFTP key exposed on the integration host
T-002.impact: The extract holds every employee's salary, bank account and tax file number. Its loss would be a notifiable data breach, and a stolen key would let someone feed PayStream false data.

T-003.title: Payment file altered between PayStream and the bank
T-003.impact: Salaries could be redirected to an attacker's account in a single pay run, with direct financial loss and staff not being paid.

T-004.title: Forged or replayed payroll journals to the general ledger
T-004.impact: False payroll figures in the ledger would distort financial reporting and take effort to find and reverse.

T-005.title: Vendor support access to payroll data goes unseen
T-005.impact: Northwind would not know if its payroll data were viewed or taken through the vendor's support channel, and could not meet its own breach notification duties.

T-006.title: Leaver accounts stay active in PayStream
T-006.impact: Former staff could keep access to payslips, and former payroll staff to administration, after they leave.

C-003.title: Extract archived for thirty days after transfer

C-004.title: Dual approval in the bank portal

test_plan.objective: Show whether an attacker could take control of payroll administration, read the nightly employee extract, or change payroll journals and payments, and whether the controls Northwind relies on would stop them.
test_plan.approach: Grey-box: the tester has this report, the architecture diagram and test accounts. Testing is limited to what Northwind runs or configures; PayStream's own platform is covered by vendor assurance.
in_scope: Northwind's PayStream tenant configuration and accounts, within PayStream's published testing policy
The integration host and its extract job
The payroll administrator's workstation and the payment file handling process
out_of_scope: PayStream's platform, data store and other tenants
Vendor support access (T-005), which is addressed by the assurance request V-005

paths.title: Take over payroll administration through an account outside single sign-on
paths.objective: Gain administrator access to the PayStream tenant without passing Entra ID multi-factor authentication.
paths.start: A corporate network position and no credentials; then repeated with the credentials of a test account set up as a leaver.
test_cases: Attempt to sign in to the administration console with a local account, bypassing single sign-on, from inside and outside the corporate network.
Test the local sign-in for lockout, password policy and whether multi-factor authentication can be skipped.
Disable a test user in Entra ID, then check whether its PayStream session and local password still work.
With administrator access, establish what can be read and changed: bank details, pay rates, and the payment file.
paths.success: Administrator access is obtained without multi-factor authentication, or a disabled user still reaches payroll data.

paths.title: Post a forged payroll journal to the general ledger
paths.objective: Create or replay a journal entry that the general ledger accepts as coming from PayStream.
paths.start: A network position from which the journal endpoint is reachable, and one captured genuine journal request.
test_cases: Send an unsigned journal request to the endpoint from an allowed address.
Replay a captured journal request unchanged, then with an altered amount.
Check whether the address restriction can be bypassed from other hosts on the corporate network.
paths.success: The general ledger accepts a journal that PayStream did not send.

paths.title: Read the employee extract or reuse the SFTP key from the integration host
paths.objective: Obtain the full employee extract, or the key that uploads it, from the integration host.
paths.start: A standard corporate user account with no rights on the integration host; then a low-privilege account on the host.
test_cases: Enumerate who can sign in to the integration host and read the service account's files.
Locate the SFTP private key and check its file permissions and whether it has a passphrase.
Locate archived extract files and check who can read them.
With the key, check what the SFTP account can list, download or overwrite at the vendor endpoint (upload of a marked test file only).
paths.success: A user other than the service account can read an extract or the private key.
paths.notes: Uploading to the SFTP endpoint needs PayStream's agreement. Use a marked test file, never a real extract.

paths.title: Alter the payment file before it reaches the bank
paths.objective: Change payee account details in the payment file without the approver noticing.
paths.start: User-level access to the payroll administrator's workstation.
test_cases: Establish where the payment file is saved and who can modify it between download and upload.
Alter a test payment file and walk it through the approval step in a test pay run, without releasing a payment.
Check whether the approver sees payee details or only totals.
paths.success: An altered file reaches the approval step and the change is not visible to the approver.
paths.notes: Process test with the payroll team present. The bank portal itself is not tested.
